brief: UBS's European morning note is primarily a market recap, not an argued thesis. US markets traded sideways after the European close (S&P +60bps, Nasdaq +1.2%). Brent crude fell 1.6% to $114 as Iran's Mojtaba Khamenei called for pursuing conditions set by Iranian officials to end the war. October consumer confidence rose unexpectedly for the first time in four months on brighter job-market and business-condition views. GOOG and MSFT report after today's close. UBS's one argued call is its FOMC base case: rates hold unchanged tonight, likely by a 10-2 vote, because the inflation problem is sticky around 3% rather than accelerating or the economy overheating, and because of proximity to the mid-term elections, which together reduce the urgency to hike immediately, even as Warsh keeps a hawkish 'more work to do' message. Asian equities climbed the most in a week, with the MSCI Asia Pacific Index up 1.5% and Kospi up 7% on Korean chipmaker strength. HSI and CSI300 also rose. UBS's London desk saw a quiet session yesterday, a pause in elevated flows, with buyers of EM and of FTSE/OMX. The UK Budget and US wholesale inventories data (Sep, 0.5%) are due at 12:30.
